q: We develop StateHarness, a runtime framework that maintains, updates, and returns this state to subsequent coding decisions
r: EC5: a new training-free runtime framework tested on existing benchmarks (RefactorBench, LHTB, ChainSWE) with nothing new for the evaluation method.

q: we present MemDev-Bench to evaluate how memory systems affect code agents over diverse repository histories
r: Include: new benchmark evaluating the effect of memory systems (a context mechanism) on Claude Code, with repeated runs and cost/steps metrics; group (b) is not narrowed by EC6.

q: We introduce a writer–evaluator framework that evolves successful and failed experience into procedural and recovery skills
r: Include: agent skill documents (context mechanism) evaluated across two harnesses incl. Claude Code and three models; group (b) is not narrowed by EC5/EC6.

q: We propose Skill Dreaming, an end-to-end framework that builds repository-specific skill libraries from PR histories
r: Include: repository-specific skill libraries guiding coding agents, with efficiency analysis; group (b) is not narrowed by EC5/EC6.

q: explicit rules override conflicting repository precedent more reliably than examples
r: Include: controlled trials of how rules in the harness's native instruction file versus code examples steer coding agents on feature tasks.

q: We introduce MUSE, a memory management framework combining multi-level memory with selective runtime injection for scientific coding agents.
r: EC5: a new memory framework for scientific coding agents tested on existing benchmarks, adding nothing to the evaluation method (also one specialised domain).

q: enforcing engineering contracts during agent execution produced no oracle-detected violation in 104 paired runs
r: Include: controlled studies with repetitions comparing rules as prompt/instruction text, post-generation checks and enforced contracts on coding agents.

q: we present Hedwig, a CLI coding agent that dynamically adjusts its autonomy level based on developer-agent interactions across sessions.
r: EC5: the contribution is a new coding agent with a small walkthrough evaluation, nothing for the evaluation method.

q: we propose the Gatekeeper Protocol, a domain-agnostic framework
r: EC5: a new agent-system interaction protocol compared with context-management baselines; sells a technique, not an evaluation method.

q: ToM-SWE, a framework that augments software engineering agents with theory-of-mind capabilities for modeling and adapting to individual users.
r: EC5: main contribution is a new agent (ToM-SWE) on SWE-style tasks; the benchmark is secondary and the tasks are issue-repair style.
